cim: Do artificial intelligence pilot zones improve air quality? Evidence from Chinese urban panel data
cim_eredeti: Do artificial intelligence pilot zones improve air quality? Evidence from Chinese urban panel data
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence, as a key driver of new quality productive forces, has received increasing attention for its potential role in environmental governance. Using China’s national pilot zones for the innovative development of new-generation artificial intelligence as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the effects of the policy on six major air pollutants based on panel data from 273 prefecture-level cities from 2009 to 2023 and a multi-period difference-in-differences approach. The results show that the policy reduced PM10 and PM2.5 concentrations by approximately 10.1% and 4.3%, respectively, while no significant effects are found for other pollutants. The findings are robust to alternative identification strategies and a range of sensitivity tests. Green technology innovation provides a potential transmission pathway, with the strongest evidence found for PM2.5, while the moderating role of pre-policy economic development is also concentrated mainly on PM2.5. These findings provide new evidence on the environmental effects of AI-oriented policies and highlight the importance of green innovation and local economic conditions in realizing their environmental benefits.
